claim: SIRT6 is an NAD+-dependent histone H3 deacetylase.
source: Sirtuin 6 (SIRT6) is an NAD+-dependent histone H3 deacetylase that is prominently found associated with chromatin, attenuates transcriptionally active promoters and regulates DNA repair, metabolic homeostasis and lifespan.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is supported by citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: SIRT6 is prominently found associated with chromatin.
source: Sirtuin 6 (SIRT6) is an NAD+-dependent histone H3 deacetylase that is prominently found associated with chromatin, attenuates transcriptionally active promoters and regulates DNA repair, metabolic homeostasis and lifespan.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citation to Michishita et al., 2005 in the introduction.

claim: SIRT6 attenuates transcriptionally active promoters.
source: Sirtuin 6 (SIRT6) is an NAD+-dependent histone H3 deacetylase that is prominently found associated with chromatin, attenuates transcriptionally active promoters and regulates DNA repair, metabolic homeostasis and lifespan.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by multiple citations in the introduction.

claim: SIRT6 regulates DNA repair.
source: Sirtuin 6 (SIRT6) is an NAD+-dependent histone H3 deacetylase that is prominently found associated with chromatin, attenuates transcriptionally active promoters and regulates DNA repair, metabolic homeostasis and lifespan.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction (Mao et al., 2011; McCord et al., 2009).

claim: SIRT6 regulates metabolic homeostasis.
source: Sirtuin 6 (SIRT6) is an NAD+-dependent histone H3 deacetylase that is prominently found associated with chromatin, attenuates transcriptionally active promoters and regulates DNA repair, metabolic homeostasis and lifespan.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: SIRT6 regulates lifespan.
source: Sirtuin 6 (SIRT6) is an NAD+-dependent histone H3 deacetylase that is prominently found associated with chromatin, attenuates transcriptionally active promoters and regulates DNA repair, metabolic homeostasis and lifespan.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by multiple citations in the introduction (Kanfi et al., 2012; Zhang et al., 2018; Roichman et al., 2021; Tian et al., 2019).

claim: SIRT6 has low affinity to free histone tails.
source: Unlike other sirtuins, it has low affinity to free histone tails but demonstrates strong binding to nucleosomes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citation to Jiang et al., 2013 in the introduction.

claim: SIRT6 demonstrates strong binding to nucleosomes.
source: Unlike other sirtuins, it has low affinity to free histone tails but demonstrates strong binding to nucleosomes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations (Gil et al., 2013; Liu et al., 2020).

claim: The zinc finger domain of SIRT6 associates tightly with the acidic patch of the nucleosome through multiple arginine anchors.
source: The zinc finger domain of SIRT6 associates tightly with the acidic patch of the nucleosome through multiple arginine anchors.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by structural data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: The Rossmann fold domain binds to the terminus of the looser DNA half of the nucleosome.
source: The Rossmann fold domain binds to the terminus of the looser DNA half of the nucleosome, detaching two turns of the DNA from the histone octamer and placing the NAD+ binding pocket close to the DNA exit site.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by structural data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: SIRT6 binding detaches two turns of the DNA from the histone octamer.
source: The Rossmann fold domain binds to the terminus of the looser DNA half of the nucleosome, detaching two turns of the DNA from the histone octamer and placing the NAD+ binding pocket close to the DNA exit site.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by structural data shown in Figure 2 and Figure 1—figure supplement 5b.

claim: SIRT6 binding places the NAD+ binding pocket close to the DNA exit site.
source: The Rossmann fold domain binds to the terminus of the looser DNA half of the nucleosome, detaching two turns of the DNA from the histone octamer and placing the NAD+ binding pocket close to the DNA exit site.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by structural data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The Rossmann fold domain shows flexibility with respect to the fixed zinc finger.
source: This domain shows flexibility with respect to the fixed zinc finger and moves with, but also relative to, the unwrapped DNA terminus.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by cryoDRGN analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: The active site of SIRT6 is perfectly poised to catalyze deacetylation of the H3 histone tail.
source: We apply molecular dynamics simulations of the histone tails in the nucleosome to show that in this mode of interaction, the active site of SIRT6 is perfectly poised to catalyze deacetylation of the H3 histone tail and that the partial unwrapping of the DNA allows even lysines close to the H3 core to reach the enzyme.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by MD simulations shown in Figure 4.

claim: The partial unwrapping of the DNA allows even lysines close to the H3 core to reach the enzyme.
source: We apply molecular dynamics simulations of the histone tails in the nucleosome to show that in this mode of interaction, the active site of SIRT6 is perfectly poised to catalyze deacetylation of the H3 histone tail and that the partial unwrapping of the DNA allows even lysines close to the H3 core to reach the enzyme.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by MD simulations shown in Figure 4e.

claim: Sirtuin is an evolutionarily conserved family of lysine deacetylases that comprises seven members in humans.
source: Sirtuin is an evolutionarily conserved family of lysine deacetylases that comprises seven members in humans and plays an important role in regulating numerous physiological and pathological processes including aging, cancer, inflammation, and metabolism (Cen et al., 2011; Vitiello et al., 2017; Wątroba et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Sirtuins play an important role in regulating aging, cancer, inflammation, and metabolism.
source: Sirtuin is an evolutionarily conserved family of lysine deacetylases that comprises seven members in humans and plays an important role in regulating numerous physiological and pathological processes including aging, cancer, inflammation, and metabolism (Cen et al., 2011; Vitiello et al., 2017; Wątroba et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Sirtuins carry out their enzymatic reaction by transferring the acetyl group to an essential NAD+ cofactor.
source: Unlike other lysine deacetylases, sirtuins carry out their enzymatic reaction by transferring the acetyl group to an essential NAD+ cofactor before acetylating the target protein (Imai et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: SIRT6 is a transcription repressor through its histone H3 deacetylation at gene promoters.
source: Through its histone H3 deacetylation at gene promoters, it is a transcription repressor attenuating inter-alia ribosome biogenesis (Sebastián et al., 2012), glycolysis (Taylor et al., 2022) and the expression of various transcription factors, including nuclear factor κB (NF-κB; Kawahara et al., 2009) and hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α; Zhong et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: SIRT6 attenuates ribosome biogenesis.
source: Through its histone H3 deacetylation at gene promoters, it is a transcription repressor attenuating inter-alia ribosome biogenesis (Sebastián et al., 2012), glycolysis (Taylor et al., 2022) and the expression of various transcription factors, including nuclear factor κB (NF-κB; Kawahara et al., 2009) and hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α; Zhong et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: SIRT6 attenuates glycolysis.
source: Through its histone H3 deacetylation at gene promoters, it is a transcription repressor attenuating inter-alia ribosome biogenesis (Sebastián et al., 2012), glycolysis (Taylor et al., 2022) and the expression of various transcription factors, including nuclear factor κB (NF-κB; Kawahara et al., 2009) and hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α; Zhong et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: SIRT6 attenuates the expression of nuclear factor κB (NF-κB).
source: Through its histone H3 deacetylation at gene promoters, it is a transcription repressor attenuating inter-alia ribosome biogenesis (Sebastián et al., 2012), glycolysis (Taylor et al., 2022) and the expression of various transcription factors, including nuclear factor κB (NF-κB; Kawahara et al., 2009) and hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α; Zhong et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: SIRT6 attenuates the expression of hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α).
source: Through its histone H3 deacetylation at gene promoters, it is a transcription repressor attenuating inter-alia ribosome biogenesis (Sebastián et al., 2012), glycolysis (Taylor et al., 2022) and the expression of various transcription factors, including nuclear factor κB (NF-κB; Kawahara et al., 2009) and hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α; Zhong et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: SIRT6 H3K9 deacetylation of telomeric chromatin maintains telomere integrity.
source: Its H3K9 deacetylation of telomeric chromatin maintains telomere integrity (Michishita et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: SIRT6 fosters DNA double-strand break repair via ADP-ribosylation of PARP1.
source: In addition, via its second enzymatic activity, ADP-ribosylation of PARP1 (Mao et al., 2011) and by stabilizing DNA-PK on chromatin (McCord et al., 2009), SIRT6 also fosters DNA double-strand break repair.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: SIRT6 fosters DNA double-strand break repair by stabilizing DNA-PK on chromatin.
source: In addition, via its second enzymatic activity, ADP-ribosylation of PARP1 (Mao et al., 2011) and by stabilizing DNA-PK on chromatin (McCord et al., 2009), SIRT6 also fosters DNA double-strand break repair.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Knockout of SIRT6 in mice leads to a shortened lifespan and a premature aging-like phenotype.
source: In mice, knockout of SIRT6 leads to a shortened lifespan and a premature aging-like phenotype (Kanfi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: SIRT6 deficiency in monkeys leads to shortened lifespan and premature aging-like phenotype.
source: Similar observations were made in monkeys deficient for the enzyme (Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Overexpression of SIRT6 extends lifespan and diminishes frailty in mice.
source: Conversely, overexpression of SIRT6 extends lifespan and diminishes frailty in mice (Roichman et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: There is a positive correlation between SIRT6 ability to promote DNA double-strand break repair and longevity in rodent species.
source: Furthermore, a study with several rodent species found a positive correlation between SIRT6 ability to promote DNA double-strand break repair and longevity - in other words, more active SIRT6 leads to longer lifespan (Tian et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: In some malignancies SIRT6 plays a role as a tumor suppressor.
source: However, whereas in some malignancies SIRT6 plays a role as a tumor suppressor (Marquardt et al., 2013; Min et al., 2012; Sebastián et al., 2012), in others it acts as an oncogene (Bauer et al., 2012; Khongkow et al., 2013; Liu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: In some malignancies SIRT6 acts as an oncogene.
source: However, whereas in some malignancies SIRT6 plays a role as a tumor suppressor (Marquardt et al., 2013; Min et al., 2012; Sebastián et al., 2012), in others it acts as an oncogene (Bauer et al., 2012; Khongkow et al., 2013; Liu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: SIRT6 is a 37 KDa protein composed of two globular parts, a Rossmann fold domain and a zinc finger domain.
source: SIRT6 is a 37 KDa protein composed of two globular parts, a Rossmann fold domain that harbors the NAD+ binding site and a zinc finger domain (Pan et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: The Rossmann fold domain of SIRT6 harbors the NAD+ binding site.
source: SIRT6 is a 37 KDa protein composed of two globular parts, a Rossmann fold domain that harbors the NAD+ binding site and a zinc finger domain (Pan et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: SIRT6 has a splayed zinc finger.
source: A striking difference between SIRT6 and other members of the sirtuin family is the presence of a splayed zinc finger and the lack of a stabilizing helix bundle linking the two globular domains.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: SIRT6 lacks a stabilizing helix bundle linking the two globular domains.
source: A striking difference between SIRT6 and other members of the sirtuin family is the presence of a splayed zinc finger and the lack of a stabilizing helix bundle linking the two globular domains.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The absence of a stabilizing helix bundle probably endows SIRT6 with a unique flexibility between the domains.
source: This absence probably endows SIRT6 with a unique flexibility between the domains (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a probable consequence and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: SIRT6 has very low activity on acetylated free H3 histones or histone peptides.
source: Unlike other sirtuins, SIRT6 has very low activity on acetylated free H3 histones or histone peptides (Jiang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: SIRT6 is nuclear and found mainly associated with chromatin.
source: This seemed to contradict findings concerning the function of SIRT6, in particular data demonstrating its activity in vivo as H3 deacetylase (Michishita et al., 2008) as well as the fact that SIRT6 is nuclear and found mainly associated with chromatin (Michishita et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Nucleosomes dramatically enhance SIRT6 enzyme activity toward acetylated H3 histones.
source: The conundrum was settled when it was revealed that nucleosomes, the in vivo cognate substrate of SIRT6, dramatically enhance the enzyme activity toward acetylated H3 histones (Gil et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: SIRT6 binds nucleosomes with high affinity via multiple interacting sites.
source: Further biochemical analysis showed that SIRT6 binds nucleosomes with high affinity via multiple interacting sites (Liu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: The structure of human SIRT6 bound to the nucleosome was obtained at 2.9 Å overall resolution for the nucleosome.
source: We obtained a single particle cryogenic electron microscopy structure showing the nucleosome at 2.9 Å overall resolution and a protein density bound to its disc-like surface (Figure 1a and Figure 1—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in the figures.

claim: The zinc finger domain of SIRT6 is resolved at 3.0 Å resolution.
source: SIRT6 could be fitted into this density with its zinc finger domain (resolved at 3.0 Å resolution), associated with the acidic patch of the nucleosome and its Rossmann fold domain (4.0–6.0 Å resolution) interacting with the DNA terminus at superhelix locations (SHL) 6 and 7 (Figure 1b and Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The Rossmann fold domain of SIRT6 is resolved at 4.0–6.0 Å resolution.
source: SIRT6 could be fitted into this density with its zinc finger domain (resolved at 3.0 Å resolution), associated with the acidic patch of the nucleosome and its Rossmann fold domain (4.0–6.0 Å resolution) interacting with the DNA terminus at superhelix locations (SHL) 6 and 7 (Figure 1b and Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The Rossmann fold domain of SIRT6 interacts with the DNA terminus at superhelix locations (SHL) 6 and 7.
source: SIRT6 could be fitted into this density with its zinc finger domain (resolved at 3.0 Å resolution), associated with the acidic patch of the nucleosome and its Rossmann fold domain (4.0–6.0 Å resolution) interacting with the DNA terminus at superhelix locations (SHL) 6 and 7 (Figure 1b and Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1.

claim: The active site of SIRT6 is positioned just above where the H3 tail enters the nucleosome disc between the two DNA gyres.
source: The active site of SIRT6 is thus positioned just above where the H3 tail enters the nucleosome disc between the two DNA gyres.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1.

claim: SIRT6 is bound predominantly at the 'right' TA-poor arm of the Widom-601 sequence where DNA interactions with the histone octamer are looser.
source: We find that SIRT6 is bound predominantly at the 'right' TA-poor arm of the Widom-601 sequence where DNA interactions with the histone octamer are looser (Ngo et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5a.

claim: A small population has a second SIRT6 bound at the 'left' TA-rich tight arm.
source: We detect however a small population with a second SIRT6 bound at the 'left' TA-rich tight arm (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Where the SIRT6 Rossmann fold binds, DNA is pulled away and detached from the histone octamer.
source: First, we find that where the SIRT6 Rossmann fold binds, DNA is pulled away and detached from the histone octamer (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2b.

claim: The Rossmann fold moves with and is attached to the DNA whereas the zinc finger domain remains fixed at the acidic patch of the nucleosome.
source: The Rossmann fold moves with and is attached to the DNA whereas the zinc finger domain remains fixed at the acidic patch of the nucleosome (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2c.

claim: In the full extent of the DNA movement, two turns from SHL 6 and 7 are detached from the histone octamer.
source: In the full extent of the DNA movement, two turns from SHL 6 and 7 are detached from the histone octamer.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2.

claim: SIRT6 binding alters the path of the terminus DNA by 37°.
source: This alters the path of the terminus DNA by 37° and breaks DNA interactions with histones H2A, H2B, and H3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 5b).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5b.

claim: SIRT6 binding breaks DNA interactions with histones H2A, H2B, and H3.
source: This alters the path of the terminus DNA by 37° and breaks DNA interactions with histones H2A, H2B, and H3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 5b).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5b.

claim: The DNA terminus without bound SIRT6 or free nucleosomes did not show any deviation from the canonical conformations.
source: Importantly, the DNA terminus without bound SIRT6 or free nucleosomes in our dataset did not show any deviation from the canonical conformations (Figure 1—figure supplement 5c).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5c.

claim: MD simulations indicate higher flexibility of the DNA termini when SIRT6 is bound to the nucleosome.
source: In addition, our MD simulations indicate higher flexibility of the DNA termini when SIRT6 is bound to the nucleosome (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The DNA movement observed is coupled to SIRT6 interactions.
source: All together these findings strongly suggest that the DNA movement we observed is coupled to SIRT6 interactions.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on multiple lines of evidence.

claim: In particles where the SIRT6-bound DNA remains in its canonical position, shifts by up to 20 Å in the position of the Rossmann fold domain of SIRT6 are observed.
source: Second, in particles where the SIRT6-bound DNA remains in its canonical position, we observe shifts by up to 20 Å in the position of the Rossmann fold domain of SIRT6, partially loosening its association with the DNA (Figure 2e and f).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2e and f.

claim: The shift of the Rossmann fold domain could be involved in fine tuning the position of the active site relative to the H3 tail.
source: We show that this shift could be involved in fine tuning the position of the active site relative to the H3 tail.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by analysis in Figure 4.

claim: The conformational changes are made possible by a flexible hinge region between the two domains of SIRT6.
source: These conformational changes are made possible by a flexible hinge region between the two domains of SIRT6, which is unique to this member of the sirtuins family.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: R175 of SIRT6 serves as a classical 'arginine anchor motif', binding to the acidic triad of E61, D90 and E92 from H2A.
source: R175 packs against H2B L103 and serves as a classical 'arginine anchor motif' (McGinty and Tan, 2016), binding to the acidic triad of E61, D90 and E92 from H2A.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation and shown in Figure 3a.

claim: R172 of SIRT6 contacts E56 and Q24 of H2A as well as Q44 and E110 of H2B.
source: SIRT6 presents two other arginines, R172, to contact E56 and Q24 of H2A as well as Q44 and E110 of H2B and R178 to contact H2A E91 and E102 from H2B.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3a.

claim: R178 of SIRT6 contacts H2A E91 and E102 from H2B.
source: SIRT6 presents two other arginines, R172, to contact E56 and Q24 of H2A as well as Q44 and E110 of H2B and R178 to contact H2A E91 and E102 from H2B.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3a.

claim: K170 of SIRT6 interacts with E64 and N68 from H2A.
source: Finally, K170 interacts with E64 and N68 from H2A (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3a.

claim: Substituting R175, R172, R178, and K170 to alanines (SIRT6-4A) significantly weakened the interaction of SIRT6 with the nucleosomes.
source: Substituting these four positively charged residues to alanines (SIRT6-4A) significantly weakened the interaction of SIRT6 with the nucleosomes as shown by electrophoretic gel-shift assay (Figure 3—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1a.

claim: SIRT6-4A mutant protein showed strongly diminished activity in deacetylating H3K9Ac.
source: The mutant protein showed strongly diminished activity in deacetylating H3K9Ac, further corroborating the role of the four basic residues R175, R172, R178, and K170, in binding to the nucleosome (Figure 3—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1b.

claim: The four positive residues of SIRT6 that bind the nucleosome acidic patch are conserved among vertebrates but not present in other human sirtuins.
source: It is important to note that the four positive residues of SIRT6 that bind the nucleosome acidic patch are conserved among vertebrates but in contrast are not present in other human sirtuins (Figure 3b and c).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3b and c.

claim: SIRT6 is the only sirtuin predominantly associated with chromatin.
source: This probably reflects the fact that SIRT6 is the only sirtuin predominantly associated with chromatin.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the conservation pattern.

claim: Three highly conserved arginines from the Rossmann fold domain (R220, R231, R248) bind the phosphate backbone at SHL 6 and 7 of the nucleosomal DNA.
source: We find that three highly conserved arginines from the Rossmann fold domain (R220, R231, R248) bind the phosphate backbone at SHL 6 and 7 of the nucleosomal DNA (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3d.

claim: The intrinsically disordered C-terminal domain of SIRT6 is necessary for establishing tight interaction of SIRT6 with the nucleosome via its ability to bind DNA.
source: A biochemical study suggests that the intrinsically disordered C-terminal domain of SIRT6 is necessary for establishing tight interaction of SIRT6 with the nucleosome (Liu et al., 2020) via its ability to bind DNA.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: A SIRT6 mutant where R220, R231, and R248 are substituted to alanines (SIRT6-3A) has severely diminished H3K9Ac deacetylase activity.
source: Indeed, applying SAGA-acetylated nucleosomes as substrates, we find that a SIRT6 mutant, where the three arginines are substituted to alanines (SIRT6-3A), has severely diminished H3K9Ac deacetylase activity (Figure 3—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1b.

claim: The three arginines R220, R231, and R248 are required to correctly position the Rossmann fold, and hence the catalytic site, with respect to the H3 tail.
source: We propose however that the three arginines are required to correctly position the Rossmann fold, and hence the catalytic site, with respect to the H3 tail.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a proposal based on the mutant data.

claim: SIRT6 binds NAD+ in the absence of an acetylated substrate.
source: Unlike other sirtuins, SIRT6 binds NAD+ in the absence of an acetylated substrate (Imai et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: Crystal structures of SIRT6 describe a rigid helix (α3) where other sirtuins contain a flexible cofactor binding loop.
source: This is attributed to the fact that crystal structures of SIRT6 describe a rigid helix (α3) where other sirtuins contain a flexible cofactor binding loop (Pan et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: Helix α3 is not observed in the cryo-EM map of SIRT6 bound to nucleosome.
source: In our map, we do not observe helix α3 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2b) and we speculate that in the context of the nucleosome, this helix assumes a flexible loop conformation that like in other sirtuins will bind the cofactor only after stabilization by the acetyl lysine substrate.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2b.

claim: In the context of the nucleosome, helix α3 of SIRT6 assumes a flexible loop conformation that will bind the cofactor only after stabilization by the acetyl lysine substrate.
source: In our map, we do not observe helix α3 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2b) and we speculate that in the context of the nucleosome, this helix assumes a flexible loop conformation that like in other sirtuins will bind the cofactor only after stabilization by the acetyl lysine substrate.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as speculation based on the absence of density.

claim: The N-terminal part of the Rossmann fold domain associates with the C-terminal tail of histone H2A at residue K119.
source: In addition, we find that the N-terminal part of the Rossmann fold domain associates with the C-terminal tail of histone H2A at residue K119 (Figure 3e).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3e.

claim: Monoubiquitination of H2A at K119 could interfere with the binding of SIRT6 or regulate its activity.
source: This observation suggests that monoubiquitination of H2A at this position, a major histone modification in mammalian cells, could interfere with the binding of SIRT6 or regulate its activity.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a suggestion based on the observed interaction.

claim: Binding of SIRT6 to nucleosomes is mildly but statistically significantly stronger when H2A.Z is incorporated instead of H2A.
source: Surprisingly, we find that binding of SIRT6 to nucleosomes is mildly (but statistically significant) stronger when H2A.Z is incorporated instead of H2A (Figure 3f and Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3f and Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: H2A.Z is enriched in nucleosomes that flank the transcription start site.
source: This finding could be related to SIRT6's role in repressing gene expression because H2A.Z is enriched in nucleosomes that flank the transcription start site.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a possible connection.

claim: Recent NMR studies and molecular dynamics predictions show that the H3 tail collapses onto the nucleosome core, driven by robust interactions with DNA.
source: However, recent NMR studies and molecular dynamics predictions show that the tail actually collapses onto the nucleosome core, driven by robust interactions with DNA (Ikebe et al., 2016; Stützer et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: The H3 tail adopts multiple structurally heterogeneous, but energetically similar, states.
source: The tail adopts multiple structurally heterogeneous, but energetically similar, states.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on cited studies.

claim: The H3 tail dynamically transitions between conformations that all interact with the last superhelix location of nucleosomal DNA.
source: It dynamically transitions between these conformations that all interact with the last superhelix location of nucleosomal DNA (Morrison et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: In several H3 conformations, the tail is located in close proximity (<15 Å) to the SIRT6 active site.
source: We find that in several H3 conformations, the tail is located in close proximity (<15 Å) to the SIRT6 active site.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4c and d.

claim: In some H3 conformations, H3K9 or H3K18 are practically situated in the active site of SIRT6.
source: In some of these cases, H3K9 or H3K18, the main target residues of SIRT6 (Wang et al., 2016), are practically situated in the active site.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation and shown in Figure 4a and b.

claim: The shift of the Rossmann fold domain draws the active site closer to the target residues in some H3 conformations.
source: Furthermore, when analyzing the two endpoints of the Rossmann fold domain shift with respect to the DNA, we observe that in some H3 conformations, this shift draws the active site closer to the target residues (Figure 4c and d).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4c and d.

claim: The high-affinity binding of SIRT6 to the nucleosome poises the active site to trapping its main target residues.
source: We conclude that the high-affinity binding of SIRT6 to the nucleosome poises the active site to trapping its main target residues.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the MD analysis.

claim: The flexibility between the Rossmann fold and Zn-finger domains serves as a fine-tuning mechanism that allows for short-range scanning of the tail in order to locate the acetylated residues.
source: In addition, the flexibility between the Rossmann fold and Zn-finger domains serves as a fine-tuning mechanism that allows for short-range scanning of the tail in order to locate the acetylated residues.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the analysis.

claim: Except H3 no other histone is present at the vicinity of the SIRT6 active site.
source: We note also that except H3 no other histone is present at the vicinity of the SIRT6 active site.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the structure.

claim: The absence of other histones at the vicinity of the SIRT6 active site gives rise to selectivity of SIRT6 toward the H3 tail.
source: This gives rise to selectivity of SIRT6 toward the H3 tail.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the structural observation.

claim: New H3 tail conformations appear in MD simulations with bound SIRT6 that are absent from a control run with nucleosome alone.
source: Strikingly, new H3 tail conformations appear in the simulations that are absent from a control run with nucleosome alone.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on MD simulations.

claim: New H3 tail pathways have the H3 tail protruding out of the histone core through the space between the DNA and the octamer that is formed via partial unwrapping of the DNA by SIRT6.
source: These pathways have the H3 tail protruding out of the histone core through the space between the DNA and the octamer that is formed via partial unwrapping of the DNA by SIRT6.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4e.

claim: In the new H3 tail conformations, the tail does not need to circle around the DNA to reach SIRT6 and therefore lysines that are closer to the core of H3 (e.g., K27) could be accessible to the enzyme.
source: Importantly, in these additional conformations H3 tail does not need to circle around the DNA to reach SIRT6 and therefore lysines that are closer to the core of H3 (e.g., K27) could also be accessible to the enzyme (Figure 4e).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4e.

claim: SIRT6 can efficiently deacetylate H3K27Ac, although at a somewhat slower rate than H3K9Ac.
source: We find that indeed SIRT6 could efficiently deacetylate H3K27Ac, although at a somewhat slower rate than H3K9Ac.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4f and Figure 3—figure supplement 1c.

claim: Partial DNA unwrapping by SIRT6 allows H3-tail conformations that make lysines that are close to the core of H3 accessible to the enzyme.
source: We conclude that partial DNA unwrapping by SIRT6 allows H3-tail conformations that make lysines that are close to the core of H3 accessible to the enzyme.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the MD and experimental data.

claim: The measured turnover rate for SIRT6 on isolated H3K9 peptides is 1000 times slower than for other sirtuins.
source: It is therefore striking that the measured turnover rate for SIRT6 on isolated H3K9 peptides is 1000 slower than for other sirtuins (Jiang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a supporting citation.

claim: The activity of SIRT6 is dramatically stimulated by binding to its cognate nucleosome substrate.
source: Moreover, unlike SIRT1, the activity of SIRT6 is dramatically stimulated by binding to its cognate nucleosome substrate (Gil et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a supporting citation.

claim: Multiple interactions of SIRT6 with the nucleosome position its active site at the putative path of relatively long-lived conformations of H3 so that residues K9 and K18 of the tail spend significant time very close to, or even at, the enzyme active site.
source: We find that multiple interactions of SIRT6 with the nucleosome position its active site at the putative path of relatively long-lived conformations of H3 so that residues K9 and K18 of the tail spend significant time very close to, or even at, the enzyme active site.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the structural and MD analysis.

claim: SIRT6 moves with respect to the nucleosomal DNA allowing it to fine-tune the position of the active site to trap the target residue.
source: In addition, SIRT6 moves with respect to the nucleosomal DNA allowing it to fine-tune the position of the active site to trap the target residue.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the structural analysis.

claim: It is the binding of SIRT6 to the nucleosome and an intrinsic scanning capability that account for its much higher enzymatic efficiency on nucleosomes.
source: Hence it is the binding of SIRT6 to the nucleosome and an intrinsic scanning capability that account for its much higher enzymatic efficiency on nucleosomes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the findings.

claim: The position of SIRT6 ensures high selectivity because the space surrounding the active site is devoid of any other tails apart from H3.
source: Importantly, the position of SIRT6 also ensures high selectivity because the space surrounding the active site is devoid of any other tails apart from H3.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the structural analysis.

claim: The recognition mode of nucleosomal H3 employed by SIRT6 is reminiscent of that used by the PRC1 complex in the specific ubiquitylation of H2A Lys119.
source: The recognition mode of nucleosomal H3 employed by SIRT6 is reminiscent of that used by the PRC1 complex in the specific ubiquitylation of H2A Lys119 (McGinty et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a supporting citation.

claim: Like SIRT6, PRC1 requires a nucleosome substrate, showing no activity on an H2A-H2B dimer.
source: Like SIRT6, PRC1 requires a nucleosome substrate, showing no activity on an H2A-H2B dimer, and multiple interactions with the nucleosome position an active site in close proximity to its target residue.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a comparison.

claim: The flexibility and scanning capacity observed for SIRT6 is lacking in PRC1.
source: However, the flexibility and scanning capacity we observed for SIRT6 is lacking in PRC1 perhaps echoing the fact that its target residue is rather stable in the nucleosome compared to the H3 tail.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a comparison.

claim: The flexibility of SIRT6 was suggested to be, at least in part, responsible for its nearly undetected activity on isolated peptides.
source: It is interesting to note that the flexibility of SIRT6 that is at the root of its scanning mechanism was suggested to be, at least in part, responsible for its nearly undetected activity on isolated peptides (Pan et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a supporting citation.

claim: It is only when SIRT6 is constrained to the proximity of the target residues, through binding to the nucleosome, that its flexibility facilitates the function of the enzyme.
source: It is only when it is constrained to the proximity of the target residues, through binding to the nucleosome, that this capacity facilitates the function of the enzyme.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion.

claim: The space formed between DNA and octamer by SIRT6 binding allows for additional conformations of the H3 tail that protrudes toward SIRT6.
source: A second major conformational change observed in our 3D reconstructions is the detachment of the DNA terminus, with a bound Rossmann fold domain, from the octamer. Our molecular dynamics simulations suggest that the space formed between DNA and octamer allows for additional conformations of the H3 tail that protrudes toward SIRT6.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on MD simulations.

claim: The new H3 tail pathways do not require circling around the DNA gyre and therefore lysines that are closer to the core of H3 (e.g. K27) can reach the active site of SIRT6.
source: These new pathways do not require circling around the DNA gyre and therefore lysines that are closer to the core of H3 (e.g. K27) can reach in this way the active site of SIRT6.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the MD simulations.

claim: K56 which lies at the core of H3 within a stable helix was reported to be a target for SIRT6.
source: We note that K56 which lies at the core of H3 within a stable helix was also reported to be a target for SIRT6.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on prior reports.

claim: SIRT6 might employ additional recognition modes for its targets beyond the one described.
source: It is therefore possible that the enzyme employs additional recognition modes of its targets.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as speculation.

claim: Other H3 modifying enzymes, such as the GCN5 HAT module of SAGA and ATAC, would place their active site in a position similar to the one of SIRT6 and possibly also displace the DNA from the histone octamer.
source: Because the position of the SIRT6 active site seems to be well suited for modifying the H3 tail, it stands to reason that other H3 modifying enzymes, such as the GCN5 HAT module of SAGA and ATAC, would place their active site in a position similar to the one of SIRT6 and possibly also displace the DNA from the histone octamer.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as speculation.

claim: Gcn5 deviates from SIRT6 in having significant affinity for the H3 tail.
source: Gcn5 deviates from SIRT6 in having significant affinity for the H3 tail and therefore might pose a less stringent requirement for precise positioning of the active site or for specific conformations of the H3 tail.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a comparison.

claim: The Gcn5 recognition mode will be similar to SIRT6 but will also include some sequence specific binding.
source: Thus, we speculate the Gcn5 recognition mode will be similar to SIRT6 but will also include some sequence specific binding.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as speculation.

claim: Two studies describing the structure of SIRT6-nucleosome appeared in press while this manuscript was under review.
source: While this manuscript was under review two studies describing the structure of SIRT6-nucleosome appeared in press (Chio et al., 2023; Wang et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction.

claim: The conclusion of the two concurrent studies regarding the position of SIRT6 on the nucleosome and the unwinding of DNA by the enzyme are similar to the findings in this manuscript.
source: The conclusion of these papers regarding the position of SIRT6 on the nucleosome and the unwinding of DNA by the enzyme are similar to our findings.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction.
